finding.claim: SSRF in /logo: the only validation is a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which can be satisfied by any URL that contains that string anywhere, e.g. in the query, path, fragment or userinfo. The request is then made to an arbitrary attacker-chosen host, redirects are followed by default, and the response body is returned to the caller (non-blind).
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 (unauthenticated HTTP request parameter on /logo)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the body echoed via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:38

trace.note: /logo route registered with no auth middleware
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; it is not parsed and not host-anchored. E.g. logo=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io passes
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects and has no scheme, host or IP restriction
the response is copied back to the attacker, so internal data is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: Substring match on the raw string only; no url.Parse, no hostname equality or allowlist, no scheme check, no private/link-local IP block, and no redirect restriction (default client). The check is bypassable, so it is not an effective control. Also note that the error from http.Get is ignored, so resp can be nil (panic), which is a separate robustness issue.

verdict.guard_found: none (only strings.Contains substring check at main.go:32; no parsing, host allowlist, scheme check, or redirect restriction)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the unauthenticated "logo" param, the only guard is a bypassable substring check at main.go:32, and main.go:36 does http.Get(raw) with default redirects and main.go:38 echoes the body back; the route is registered at main.go:43, not :42 as one trace note implies, but the registration has no auth either way.
